subsystems.name: Chassis microbe
subsystems.role: the living host that carries and expresses the degradation genes.

subsystems.name: Genetic circuit
subsystems.role: controls when and how much degradation enzyme is made.

subsystems.name: Enzyme payload
subsystems.role: catalyses the breakdown of the target pollutant.

subsystems.name: Containment system
subsystems.role: prevents the engineered microbe from spreading beyond the site.

subsystems.name: Delivery and survival package
subsystems.role: helps the microbe establish and persist in contaminated soil or water.

subsystems.name: Monitoring and control
subsystems.role: tracks degradation activity and detects escape.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the pollution
buildSteps.detail: Sample the site and identify the pollutants, their concentrations (e.g., milligrams per litre in groundwater) and the physical conditions such as pH and temperature.

buildSteps.title: Choose a chassis
buildSteps.detail: Select a non-pathogenic microbe already suited to the site, such as a soil bacterium that tolerates the contaminants and local conditions.

buildSteps.title: Design the genetic circuit
buildSteps.detail: Use software to design DNA sequences that encode enzymes known to break the pollutant's chemical bonds, plus regulatory parts that switch them on only when needed.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise and assemble DNA
buildSteps.detail: Order or build the DNA fragments and insert them into the chassis using standard molecular biology techniques.

buildSteps.title: Test in the lab
buildSteps.detail: Grow the engineered microbe in microcosms — small flasks or soil columns — spiked with the pollutant, and measure how fast it disappears.

buildSteps.title: Optimise performance
buildSteps.detail: Tune gene expression, enzyme variants and growth conditions to maximise degradation while keeping the microbe safe and stable.

buildSteps.title: Contained field trial
buildSteps.detail: Release the microbe into a sealed or monitored plot to test survival, degradation rate and containment under real conditions.

buildSteps.title: Scale up production
buildSteps.detail: Grow the microbe in fermenters (thousands of litres) and formulate it into a stable product for transport.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Apply the product to the contaminated site, then sample regularly to confirm pollution levels fall and the microbe does not spread.

prerequisites.why: tools like DNA synthesis and CRISPR allow precise design of microbial genomes.
many pollutant-degrading enzymes are known, but complete pathways for recalcitrant compounds are still being discovered.
kill switches and auxotrophy work in the lab but are not yet proven over years in the open environment.
bioaugmentation and encapsulation have been tested, but delivering live microbes to deep soil or groundwater reliably is difficult.
most countries have no clear path to permit environmental release of genetically modified microorganisms.

pathway.milestone: lab strains that degrade model pollutants such as oil components or chlorinated solvents
pathway.unlocks: proof that engineered enzymes work outside the test tube.

pathway.milestone: contained field trials for a single pollutant at a specific site
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on survival, degradation and containment.

pathway.milestone: commercial bioremediation products for niche spills or industrial sites
pathway.unlocks: a market that funds further engineering.

pathway.milestone: routine use for soil and groundwater cleanup, combined with plants and natural microbes
pathway.unlocks: faster, cheaper restoration of contaminated land.
